questions.q: What does a multimeter show between CAN_H and CAN_L of a healthy bus with the power off?
questions.explain: Two 120 Ω terminators at the ends in parallel give 60 Ω; 120 means one terminator, 40 means three.

questions.q: Why does CAN tolerate a meter of wire next to the power bus while I²C does not?
options: CAN runs at a higher frequency and has time to resend the frame
CAN is differential: the interference is the same on both wires
CAN is shielded inside the connector
questions.explain: The receiver looks at the H−L difference; common-mode interference cancels out.

questions.q: A new DroneCAN node was plugged in without any setup and it works. Who gave it its ID?
options: The DNA server on the flight controller
The ID is burned in by the manufacturer and never changes
questions.explain: Dynamic node allocation: the flight controller hands out a free node ID and remembers it by the node's unique ID.

questions.q: After moving a GPS node from another vehicle, the GPS data jumps. The likely cause?
options: No terminator at the flight controller
questions.explain: The stored ID matched another node; fixed by clearing the DNA table or changing the ID.

questions.q: Which ArduPilot parameter selects DroneCAN as the protocol of the first driver?
questions.explain: CAN_P1_DRIVER enables the port and assigns a driver; CAN_D1_PROTOCOL = 1 is DroneCAN for that driver.

questions.q: The nodes are visible in Mission Planner, but the EKF gets no GPS. What do you check first?
options: The node firmware version in the list
questions.explain: A node on the bus doesn't yet mean the autopilot uses it as a GPS — the sensor type is selected explicitly.

questions.q: Eight ESCs over CAN at 400 Hz plus sensors — what's a sensible move?
options: Raise the bus bitrate to 2 Mbit/s on all nodes at once
Move the ESCs to a separate CAN2 bus
Remove the terminators to reduce the load
questions.explain: ESC commands take a noticeable share of the bandwidth; two buses split the load and give redundancy.

ArduPilot firmware for a DroneCAN node on STM32
A version of the Cyphal protocol
questions.explain: The same ArduPilot driver code built for a peripheral board — the way to your own CAN sensor.
